title: Master services agreement
subtitle: Northstar × Meridian · Technology services

items.title: 1. Parties and purpose
items.text: Northstar Analytics Ltd (Customer) appoints Meridian Digital Services Ltd (Supplier) to design, implement and support the Customer platform. This Master Services Agreement governs each signed Statement of Work. Neither forecasts nor discussions create a commitment to purchase. Each party acts as an independent contractor and cannot bind the other.
items.task: Confirm legal entities and signing authority.

items.title: 2. Order of precedence
items.text: A signed change order prevails over the affected Statement of Work, followed by that Statement of Work, the Data Processing Schedule, this Agreement and other schedules. A Statement of Work may vary liability or intellectual property terms only by naming the clause and obtaining both parties’ authorized signatures. Purchase order terms are excluded.
items.task: Verify each override explicitly identifies the affected clause.

items.title: 3. Statements of Work
items.text: Each Statement of Work shall identify deliverables, milestones, dependencies, acceptance criteria, charges, service levels and named representatives. The Supplier shall not start a chargeable milestone until the Statement of Work is signed. The Customer shall supply timely access, information and decisions listed as dependencies. Delay relief requires a written impact notice within five business days.
items.task: Signed SOW is a prerequisite to commencing work.

items.title: 4. Delivery and change control
items.text: The Supplier shall maintain a delivery plan, issue weekly status reports and escalate a forecast milestone delay within two business days. A proposed change shall state scope, cost, timing, security and dependency impacts. No change is binding before both representatives sign a change order. Pending approval, the Supplier continues unaffected work under the existing baseline.
items.task: Create a baseline and an approval gate for every change.

items.title: 5. Acceptance
items.text: The Customer has ten business days after delivery to test against the agreed acceptance criteria. A rejection must identify material non-conformities with evidence. The Supplier shall correct them within ten business days and resubmit. Silence alone does not constitute acceptance. Minor defects may be placed on an agreed remediation list without delaying acceptance of otherwise conforming deliverables.
items.task: Capture delivery date, test evidence and written acceptance.

items.title: 6. Service levels and support
items.text: Production availability shall be 99.9% per calendar month excluding agreed maintenance. Priority-one incidents require acknowledgement within thirty minutes and continuous reasonable efforts until workaround or resolution. Service credits are calculated under the service schedule and are not the exclusive remedy for repeated material failures. Monthly service reports must include incident history and corrective actions.
items.task: Track availability, incidents and recurring breach escalation.

items.title: 7. Personnel and subcontracting
items.text: The Supplier remains responsible for all personnel and approved subcontractors. Replacement of named key personnel requires prior consultation and equivalent competence. Subcontractors with access to Customer data require prior written approval, confidentiality commitments and equivalent security obligations. The Supplier shall maintain a current subcontractor register.
items.task: Approval required before a new data-access subcontractor is used.

items.title: 8. Charges, invoices and disputes
items.text: Fees are those stated in the applicable Statement of Work. Valid invoices are payable within thirty days of receipt and must identify the milestone and purchase order. The Customer may dispute an invoice in good faith within fifteen business days, paying undisputed amounts on time. Work shall not be suspended solely for a genuinely disputed amount while the escalation procedure is followed.
items.task: Validate invoice evidence and separate disputed amounts.

items.title: 9. Taxes, expenses and records
items.text: Charges exclude applicable sales taxes, which must be separately itemized. The Supplier bears taxes on its income and employment. Travel and exceptional expenses require prior written approval and receipts. The Supplier shall retain records supporting time-and-material charges for six years and permit a proportionate confidential review on reasonable notice.
items.task: Check tax allocation, approval evidence and audit retention.

items.title: 10. Warranties and insurance
items.text: The Supplier warrants reasonable skill and care, conformity with specifications, and that deliverables do not knowingly contain malicious code. It shall maintain professional indemnity insurance of USD 2 million and cyber insurance of USD 3 million during performance and for two years afterwards. Insurance does not expand or replace contractual liability.
items.task: Obtain certificates and check policy scope and expiry.

items.title: 11. Liability allocation
items.text: Each party’s aggregate liability arising in a contract year is capped at the fees paid or payable during that year. Liability for confidentiality breaches, data protection breaches and intellectual property indemnities is subject to a separate cap of two times those fees. Fraud, deliberate misconduct and liabilities that cannot legally be limited are uncapped. Neither party is liable for indirect losses, subject to the expressly recoverable direct costs in the schedules.
items.task: Escalate the annual fee cap and two-times super-cap for approval.

items.title: 12. Indemnities and claims
items.text: The Supplier shall defend a third-party claim that a deliverable infringes intellectual property rights and pay finally awarded damages and reasonable settlement amounts. The Customer must promptly notify the claim, allow defense control and provide reasonable assistance. No settlement admitting fault or imposing non-monetary obligations on the Customer may be entered without its consent. The Supplier may procure rights, replace or modify affected deliverables without reducing functionality.
items.task: Check defense control, exclusions and remedy sequence.

items.title: 13. Confidentiality
items.text: Confidential information may be used only to perform or receive services and disclosed only to personnel with a need to know and equivalent obligations. Public information, independently developed information and lawfully received information are excluded. Compelled disclosure requires advance notice where lawful. General confidentiality survives for five years; trade secrets remain protected while they retain that status.
items.task: Record permitted recipients and survival periods.

items.title: 14. Personal data and security
items.text: The Customer is controller and the Supplier processor for service personal data. Processing is limited to documented instructions in the Data Processing Schedule. Security measures include access control, encryption, logging, testing and incident procedures. The Supplier shall notify the Customer without undue delay and in any event within twenty-four hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach, with available facts and continuing updates.
items.task: Confirm roles, signed DPA and 24-hour notification process.

items.title: 15. Transfers, audit and deletion
items.text: Personal data shall remain in the agreed regions. Cross-border transfers require an approved lawful mechanism and documented assessment. The Supplier shall provide annual independent assurance and permit a risk-based audit where the assurance is insufficient. On termination, data shall be returned in an accessible format and deleted within thirty days unless retention is legally required; retained copies remain protected.
items.task: Verify transfer mechanism and collect deletion evidence.

items.title: 16. Ownership and licenses
items.text: Customer materials remain the Customer’s property. Subject to payment of the relevant undisputed fees, bespoke deliverables are assigned to the Customer on creation to the extent permitted by law. Supplier background tools remain Supplier property, with a perpetual worldwide license to the extent embedded in or necessary to use the deliverables. Third-party and open-source components must be disclosed with license restrictions before delivery.
items.task: Separate foreground IP, background tools and third-party restrictions.

items.title: 17. Term and termination
items.text: The initial term is twenty-four months. Renewal requires a written agreement at least sixty days before expiry. Either party may terminate for a material breach not remedied within thirty days after notice, or for insolvency where permitted by law. The Customer may terminate for convenience on ninety days’ notice, paying for conforming completed work and unavoidable pre-approved commitments, with no lost-profit charge for unperformed services.
items.task: Set renewal alerts and document cure and convenience notices.

items.title: 18. Exit and transition
items.text: For up to ninety days after termination the Supplier shall provide reasonable transition assistance at the agreed rates, maintain critical services where paid, export Customer data and cooperate with a replacement supplier. The Supplier shall deliver an exit inventory and a deletion certificate. Disputed invoices do not permit withholding Customer data.
items.task: Use an exit checklist with data export and deletion gates.

items.title: 19. Compliance and business continuity
items.text: Each party shall comply with applicable anti-bribery, sanctions and employment laws relevant to its performance. The Supplier shall test its business continuity and disaster recovery plans annually and provide a summary. A force majeure event requires prompt notice and mitigation; if it continues for sixty days the affected Statement of Work may be terminated without further cancellation charge.
items.task: Collect continuity evidence and define disruption escalation.

items.title: 20. Disputes and general provisions
items.text: Representatives shall attempt to resolve a dispute within ten business days, then escalate it to executives for twenty days before proceedings, without restricting urgent relief. This Agreement is governed by the fictional State of Alder law, with courts in Alder City. Notices must be sent to the designated legal addresses. Amendments require signed writing; severability, waiver, counterparts and entire-agreement provisions apply.
items.task: Replace illustrative governing law before real-world use.

title: Project Atlas · Legal due diligence
subtitle: Acquisition of a fictional software business

items.title: Articles & register
items.text: Share register shows two classes of shares; one historic transfer lacks the countersigned instrument.
items.task: Request the executed transfer and reconcile beneficial ownership.

items.title: Board approvals
items.text: Board minutes authorize the financing round but do not identify approval for a related-party agreement.
items.task: Confirm corporate authority for the related-party transaction.

items.title: Capitalization table
items.text: Option pool is 12% fully diluted. Three option grants have no matching signed grant agreement.
items.task: Reconcile option grants and obtain signed instruments.

items.title: Customer agreements
items.text: Two enterprise contracts require consent for a change of control; annual recurring revenue concentration is 38%.
items.task: Obtain customer consents and quantify revenue exposure.

items.title: Supplier agreements
items.text: Cloud services renew automatically with a sixty-day cancellation notice. No transition assistance is agreed.
items.task: Confirm renewal dates and negotiate transition arrangements.

items.title: Channel agreements
items.text: Distributor exclusivity covers three territories and survives for twelve months after termination.
items.task: Assess competition restrictions and post-close channel flexibility.

items.title: Employment agreements
items.text: Four engineering agreements omit an express invention assignment. Local statutory ownership needs verification.
items.task: Obtain assignments and verify local employment rules.

items.title: Contractor agreements
items.text: Two long-term contractors work exclusively and use company equipment. Classification requires local review.
items.task: Review status, payroll exposure and remediation options.

items.title: Incentive plans
items.text: The equity plan provides transaction acceleration subject to board discretion. Consent records are incomplete.
items.task: Calculate transaction payments and locate board approvals.

items.title: IP portfolio
items.text: Trademark renewal is due in six weeks. One core code module originated with an external development studio.
items.task: Renew the mark and verify the studio chain of title.

items.title: Open-source inventory
items.text: Inventory lists a copyleft component in a distributed build. License version and linkage have not been assessed.
items.task: Obtain a software bill of materials and analyze obligations.

items.title: Privacy & processing
items.text: A signed DPA is missing for an analytics provider. Records list international transfers without an attached assessment.
items.task: Execute the DPA and document the transfer mechanism.

items.title: Litigation schedule
items.text: A former reseller claims unpaid commission of USD 240,000. Counsel’s merits analysis is outstanding.
items.task: Request counsel assessment, pleadings and settlement authority.

items.title: Licenses & permits
items.text: The permit register contains current operating approvals but one entry has no renewal evidence.
items.task: Verify permit status with the relevant regulator.

items.title: Compliance policies
items.text: Anti-bribery training records cover 78% of staff. A whistleblower report remains open without closure evidence.
items.task: Obtain investigation status and close training gaps.
